caption:
Exciting news for girls in sports! i9 Sports is tackling the dropout crisis in girls sports. They asked parents in their youth sports programs to take a survey with their daughters and received over 1500 responses. 

The goal of the survey was to find out what parents and their daughters are looking for in a youth sports program so i9 Sports can lead the way in creating programs that girls want to play in!

i9 Sports believes they can keep girls in sports longer if they can create an environment in which girls feel like they belong. 

This survey is the first step to launching their larger
campaign—Gains are for the Girls! 

Gains are for the Girls is a promise to create greater access, opportunity, and spaces in youth sports where girls feel they can learn, grow, and thrive as athletes and as people. 

As a female athlete, I’m more than excited to share the launch of the Gains are for the Girls campaign and these survey insights. It’s awesome to see a youth sports organization making real commitments to girls in sports! #GainsFortheGirls #YouthSports #GirlsInSports  @i9_sports

WHEN TRUST, TIMING, AND A DIFFERENT KIND OF AGENT ALIGN 🏈

In a landscape where representation often comes with noise, @thetyanthonysmith chose a quieter path, trusting a newer, untraditional agent and allowing timing and preparation to do the work. That decision proved meaningful as Ty prepares to return to Texas with clarity on both his football future and the business surrounding it.

Ty’s agent, Jacob “J5” Smith, @jsmith_e4brand  might have the same name , but is not connected by name or relation, and his approach to representation reflects that difference. He leads with faith, discipline, and a spiritually grounded mindset, while still operating with sharp business instincts behind the scenes. The work was done without public posturing or unnecessary attention, focusing instead on making sure the deal aligned with Ty’s role, value, and long-term trajectory.

On the field, Ty has already demonstrated his impact, including a standout performance in the Citrus Bowl against Michigan where he recorded nine tackles, two interceptions, and a tackle for loss. Within the program, he has continued to earn trust through consistency, preparation, and leadership in the linebacker room, reinforcing why this return matters for both the player and the team.

This story isn’t about headlines or hype. It’s about what can happen when an athlete trusts timing, chooses guidance that aligns with his values, and works with someone whose strength comes from a different place. Jacob Smith’s approach may be quiet, but it carries weight, and in this case, it helped position his client exactly where he deserves to be.

I’ve been putting this off for long enough, because no amount of words will ever fully capture the gratitude I have for the girls I was lucky enough to call my teammates. These past four years truly flew by in the blink of an eye, filled with unforgettable moments, challenges that shaped us, and memories I’ll carry forever. Through every high and low, these women pushed me, believed in me, and became more than teammates—they became family. To be able to walk away from this chapter as a two-time National Champion alongside them is something I’ll cherish forever. How lucky am I to have something that makes saying goodbye so hard. 

Thank you, Longhorn nation, for taking a chance on and welcoming in a young girl from the islands. From the very beginning, this place felt like home. The support, the pride, and the traditions are unlike anything else, and I’m forever grateful to have worn the burnt orange. There truly is no place like Texas, and I will always carry a piece of this place with me wherever life takes me. 

Well, it’s been real…it’s been fun…I think you know how the rest of it goes😉

trials & tribulations 

With time all things will heal and for me it was my shoulder. In June I decided to get surgery and heal for the better of myself, my team, and my future. 

This summer/fall was a challenge mentally and physically which pushed me in different ways I may not have been ready for at times. 

My support system never lacked to give me encouragement and love to help me through these last months that were very different for me. Thank yall for everything 🤍

June 16th Surgery day 
Nov 11th I officially got cleared!!
Dec 19th I hit my first homerun with @mexicosoftball since surgery!! 

Gods timing truly never fails! I was taught lessons and patience in this time but also to always trust Gods path for me. Without him I am nothing and I thank him for the moments I got to see life in a different light.

caption:
I am not sure where to begin or how to express how much this program has meant to me over the last 3 1/2 years! Through the ups, the downs and all the in-between this program has allowed me to grow, flourish, and become a version of myself that has been shaped by all of the people who have touched my life.

To my family, the coaches, the staff, academics, the fans, and of course, my teammates and best friends, you have made this journey what it is. I have been surrounded by some of the most incredible people throughout this experience who have all taught me so much about how to love always, laugh joyfully, inspire others and grow in every facet of my life. The culture and the love that Texas volleyball possesses is nothing short of amazing and I have been so blessed to be a part of it for the last 3 1/2 years.

The reason saying goodbye is so hard is because of how good it was. 16-year-old me could’ve never imagined this being my college experience. God knew what he was doing when he put Texas on my heart and showed me countless signs as to why Texas would be my home. Thank you, Jesus for guiding me here! Texas volleyball has my heart!!

Hook ’em forever🧡🤘🏼

Throwing out my smelly knee pads for the last time is a lot harder than I could’ve ever imagined…

Ten years of dedication to a sport that’s given me more than I could’ve ever dreamed of. Thank you, @texasvolleyball, for the best four years a girl could ask for. The many memories, friendships, and lessons will stay with me forever. 🧡

To the girls just starting their volleyball journey, embrace it all. The wins, the losses, the long practices, the early mornings, and every single person you meet along the way. Most importantly, always play because you love it.

Volleyball will forever be one of my greatest joys. Though this chapter closes, I’m so excited to find ways to pour that same love and passion into the next generation of players. 

Most of all, I’m thankful to God for writing a story far greater than anything I could’ve planned for myself !

Desde que pasó,
Me he preguntado una y otra vez qué significa ser olímpica.
Más allá del talento, más allá de las expectativas,
más allá incluso del sueño que un día me desveló.

Para mí, serlo es comenzar una nueva historia,
una historia de superación, de vida,
de ver lo imposible volverse realidad,
de haber sentido el sueño entre mis manos.

Y ahora… ¿Qué sigue?
A veces es fácil desear más,
perseguir el siguiente “logro”.

¿Por qué no me detengo un momento?
Respira.
Mira hacia atrás y abraza lo que fui,
lo que soy,
lo que logré y hasta donde he llegado.
(Un abrazo al corazón)

De: Mi (mi manera de expresarme)
Para: Mi presente,

Recordatorio: El éxito sin gratitud no es éxito.

caption:
🚨 La clavadista olímpica Alejandra Estudillo se recupera exitosamente de la cirugía a la que fue sometida hace un mes del hombro izquierdo, y se dijo motivada para regresar lo más pronto posible a la plataforma, ya que su sueño es brillar este ciclo olímpico rumbo a Los Ángeles 2028. 

🎙️”Me operaron hace un mes del hombro izquierdo, porque durante mi proceso para el mundial tuve una lesión, pero gracias a Dios a pesar de eso se logró un buen resultado del cual estoy muy contenta y orgullosa”, mencionó Ale Estudillo, quien fue olímpica en París 2024 y se convirtió el pasado mes de julio en multimedallista mundial, al sumar a su cuenta personal dos preseas de plata, tras su actuación por equipos y en la plataforma sincronizados femenil. 

La pequeña valiente de los clavados, al ser la mujer con la lista de saltos de más grado de dificultad del planeta, y quien sorprendió con su talento y rápido acoplamiento como nueva pareja de la medallista olímpica Gaby Agundez, se dijo agradecida con el doctor Francisco Cruz López, quien “me ayudó con todo este proceso para la cirugía, entender mi lesión y saber cómo solucionarla”. 

Aunque parecía una lesión tipo “slap”, explicó que “a la hora que entraron se vio que no estaba tan mal, había demasiada inflamación y la ruptura del tendón no era tan grande, entonces cuando salí de la cirugía nos dieron la noticia y  me alegré muchísimo porque de pensar que duraría casi seis meses de recuperación, serán solo dos o tres meses, eso es una muy buena noticia”. 

Acompañada en todo momento por su familia, Ale Estudillo, miembro de la Secretaría de Marina y estudiante en diseño de interiores, se dijo “muy feliz, porque creo que voy avanzando muy rápido”, después de decirle adiós al cabestrillo y recuperar su movilidad casi al 100 por ciento. 

Con la disciplina y compromiso que la caracteriza a sus 20 años, se ha esforzado al máximo para superar este momento: “en mis terapias, en la escuela, que ahorita estoy llevando el proceso de rehabilitación en la Universidad de Texas y estoy muy contenta también con eso”, por lo que dijo convencida: “espero regresar lo más pronto posible”.

From intern to Olympic dream. When @yann_spillmann joined us two years ago for an internship, fresh-faced and full of promise on the 400m track, we had no idea how many times he’d go on to surprise us.

From earning his spot in the French 4x400 squad for Paris 2024 to clocking a massive PB of 45.29 and taking silver at the French Championships on last Sunday, Yann always shows up when it counts.

More than an athlete, he’s the guy who lights up the room with his energy and his endless smile.

We’re proud, we’re grateful and we’ll keep backing him all the way as he heads to the U.S. for his next chapter, books and blocks, with LA 2028 in sight.

📷 @gagastrophe @yann_spillmann

Hey y’all,
This week I’m competing in the @wgachampionships at Skokie Country Club in Chicago. In partnership with my friends at @urbangolfperformance we are each pledging $100 for every birdie I make to support the Hunt Volunteer Fire Department.
Many of my close friends and family from UT have been deeply affected by the devastating floods earlier this month. The tragedy has taken sisters, cousins, grandparents — and left communities like Hunt, Camp Mystic, and so many others across Texas reeling.
Texans are strong, and I believe we’ll do what we’ve always done in hard times — step up with a helping hand and a full heart.
If you’re able, please consider joining us. You can donate outright or pledge per birdie this week. The link to donate is in my bio.
Thank y’all. God bless Texas—and Hook ’em 🤘

caption:
MERCI BERGEN 🥹🇳🇴

Que dire… cette semaine a été remplie d’émotions, à la fois bonnes et mauvaises, mais elle restera gravée en moi pour toujours.

J’arrive à Bergen avec de grandes ambitions et l’envie d’aller chercher une médaille ce qui était plus qu’atteignable vu mon statut, mais il faut aussi savoir que je suis arrivé avec un corps qui n’était pas dans la forme de mon record personnel (20’’40), et avec un adducteur très douloureux qui m’handicape depuis un moment à l’entraînement. Bref, la mission était compliquée, mais je n’ai jamais arrêté d’y croire. J’ai mis tout en œuvre, seul (car oui, je suis seul depuis mon retour en France) pour être prêt pour le plus grand rendez-vous de ma saison… mais j’ai échoué.

C’est dur, très dur, quand on s’entraîne pour une chose pendant un an et qu’on n’y arrive pas.
Mais comme m’a dit @imadelgoumri : ceux qui pleurent et se morfondent sont ceux qui ne croient pas qu’ils peuvent faire mieux que ce qu’ils ont déjà fait.
Alors oui, c’est dur… mais on est encore loin de la fin. Je sais que des jours meilleurs m’attendent, et que tout ça arrive pour une raison. Je fais confiance au plan que Dieu a pour moi, et j’avance.

Malgré cette grosse déception, j’ai vécu une semaine incroyable, j’ai rencontré des personnes qui comptent beaucoup pour moi et j’ai créé des souvenirs qui resteront gravés très longtemps. Merci l’équipe de France pour cette semaine ❤️

Je reviendrai. 🫡

Words and pictures can’t truly capture the impact the community of Icayuco had on us last week. From shared smiles, helping hands, and meaningful cultural exchanges, every moment felt special, and those were just a small part of what made this trip unforgettable. There was so much beauty in the big moments, but just as much magic in the mundane, everyday ones. I’ve never met a community so selfless, so eager to support one another, and so committed to building a better future for the next generation. Serving this community was an absolute gift! I feel so incredibly blessed to have been part of it and work alongside such a hardworking team! I can’t wait to see how the kids now playing on this court grow into the next generation of Icayuco’s leaders and community! (And you never know, maybe some pro athletes😉!)
1 Peter 4:10-11💗

Grateful for it all @uiltexas 

Saying goodbye to this chapter of my life is harder than I imagined. High school running has been a constant—something that shaped who I am. To think it’s come to an end is bittersweet. Being a part of the Bridgeland program has taught me so much, and I’ve been lucky to grow alongside some of the most talented, dedicated individuals. This team is truly something special, and being a part of it has been one of the greatest blessings.

This past weekend, I got to toe the line one last time with one of my best friends in both the 6A State 3200 and 1600. While the races didn’t go quite how I had imagined or trained for, I’m still so grateful for the opportunity and everything this journey has given me. It’s been an incredible season, and I’ll cherish it always.

See you soon, NCAA🤘🤘

📸 @hluther07

“Different school, same goals.”

After a lot of prayer, reflection, and honest conversations with the people closest to me, I’ve decided not to attend the University of Virginia and take a new path. This wasn’t an easy decision—but it was the right one.

Sometimes the road shifts, but the vision stays the same. My goals haven’t changed—they’ve only grown louder. I’m grateful for the journey that brought me here, and even more grateful for the peace I’ve found in this next chapter.

With faith as my foundation and fire in my heart, I’m excited to announce my commitment to The University of Texas.

caption:
How incredibly blessed am I to spend the last 8 days in Italy serving and growing closer to the Lord! 

This trip with @atxaia was about learning more about Italian culture, exploring, and seeing if we would be a good connection to @athletesinactionitaly to help bring the gospel across the world to the people of Italy. We were able to serve in different communities, learn about current projects/hopes in ministry, and just meet and talk to Italians where they were at. 

This past week has taught me many things but the most clear thing on my heart was learning to be still and present with those around me. To listen and see what is happening right where I am so that I may form more meaningful and loving relationships. The hardest thing for me to take in on this trip was how Italy has such a rich Biblical history, yet so many of the people here do not know God which broke my heart. However, it was incredibly inspiring to see the few who do have faith show such optimism that the people here could come to know God, and have the aspiration everyday to go and help them do just that!

As we were here, we read through Romans and studied what Paul was trying to teach the people of Rome while he was here. What stuck on my mind and heart was the verse Romans 5:17 “For if, by the trespass of the one man, death reigned through that one man, how much more will those who receive God’s abundant provision of grace and of the gift of righteousness reign in life through the one man, Jesus Christ!” While it felt like this country was far from Christ, I reminded that God is a faithful God who can do seemingly impossible things, especially to bring us closer to Him so that he may dwell with us. 
‭
As I sit and reflect on this week, I am so grateful that the Lord provided me the opportunity to learn more about Him, serve His people, and seek His people so they may desire to know and love Him.

caption:
Yesterday I lost a piece of my heart. My Dad was one of the strongest people I will ever know. He gave me my confidence to do what ever my heart desired. I learned many things from him, one being how to love. The love for my family and friends grew deeper everyday because he loved everyone and I wanted to be just like him. I am glad I have so many memories to cherish of him. Down to making up silly dances, drawing on my lunch bags for school, cooking, and of course playing tennis. One of his all time favorite things to do was play tennis. I am so glad I have the opportunity at Texas to make him proud, I know he will be looking down watching me play.  I can’t say it enough of how awesome this man was, he did everything for his family. One thing that stuck with me was a quote he would say “Do not get comfortable with being good. Good is the enemy of great!” He would write this on pieces of paper and tape them up around my room and even slide them in my backpack. I will live everyday by this quote to be the best I can be for him. I am so proud to be his daughter. I love you daddy. 🤍

Strengthen our faith, weaken the wicked 🕊️

caption:
Wow!!! So much fun this year, even through all the ups and downs. I had much less time to prepare due to some injuries earlier this year. 

This decathlon was an absolute grind, not the way I wanted it to go, but it was still a blast to compete with all the great competition. 

I finished sixth, earning myself an all American title,  despite only scoring in NINE events. An unfortunate accident that happened in the pole vault caused me to no height. But I still finished strong and threw a PR in javelin and ran a 4:29 to win the 1500. I also hit a new day 1 PR including a PR in shot put and the 100m.

I want to thank all of my coaches, Coach Emily, @lonestar.pv, @d1boerne Mike, @jumpacademytx, and Coach Harvey, all who I couldn't have done it without. A huge thanks to @hillcountrycomets for training me to be the best I can be. A big thanks goes to coach Klim @coach_klim_penn_vertical_jumps who came out to see me from U Penn. I also want to thank my family, who have sacrificed so much for me and my goals, I can't even describe it. But most importantly I want to thank God for allowing me to be the person I am and allowing me to do what I do. 

On to the next chapter and back to the grindstone, get ready for what's coming!
